headline: Policymakers must give teachers a stronger voice on AI policy in schools, new Cambridge report recommends
snippet: New Cambridge University Press & Assessment report sets out eight key principles for effective AI integration in schools SINGAPORE, Nov. 4, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Policymakers should work closely with teachers to shape policy for the AI age in schools, and invest in comprehensive, sustained teacher professional learning to ensure educators can effectively use AI in their classrooms and critically engage with tools, a new Cambridge University Press & Assessment (Cambridge) report recommends. Crucially, teachers and learners should contribute to the design, procurement, implementation and evaluation of GenAI tools so that policy is grounded in classroom realities. The new report, 'Shaping AI Policy and Practice in English Language Teaching', draws on the best practices of English language teachers from around the world who have been early adopters of GenAI, as well as earlier Cambridge research on AI and teacher use, seeking to bring structure to an often-disjointed approach to AI use and adoption. The findings suggest many teachers globally are navigating AI, but in a vacuum, often without clear direction. Teachers' number one concern is how to support students to become AI-ready – to critically analyse AI outputs, proactively question their accuracy, and skilfully use GenAI as a tool to support, rather than shortcut, learning. To support teachers and inform policy, Cambridge sets out eight key principles for harnessing AI effectively in schools: Involve teachers and learners in AI governance. Teachers and learners should contribute to decisions about the implementation and evaluation of GenAI tools so that policy is grounded in classroom realities. Invest in sustained teacher professional learning. Teachers need ongoing support to evaluate tools critically, make informed pedagogical decisions, adapt GenAI to learning goals, and teach students responsible use. Embed critical AI literacy as a curriculum expectation. Students should learn how to question AI outputs, identify bias and inaccuracies, use GenAI as a learning support rather than a shortcut, and understand when not to use it. Critical AI literacy is essential and not an optional add-on. Reform curriculum and assessment frameworks. Curriculum and assessment systems should recognise process evidence, feedback literacy, learner reflection, and independent thinking alongside final products, in an integrated learning and assessment approach. Prioritise human-centred educational outcomes. Policy frameworks should focus on the human capabilities that need to be strengthened in the AI era, such as critical thinking, communication, autonomy, emotional intelligence and social responsibility. Build trust through ethical use and robust safeguards. Responsible integration and trust by all stakeholders, e.g., teachers, learners, parents, depends on clear approaches to data privacy, age-appropriate access, inclusivity, responsible authorship, transparency and accountability. Protect teacher agency and professional judgement. Policies should position teachers as decision-makers in tool design selection, classroom integration, evaluation and improvement – not merely as implementers of externally chosen technologies. Ensure equitable access to high-quality tools. Policy should address language diversity, local contexts, accessibility, and under-resourced settings so that GenAI does not widen existing inequalities. Dr Evelina Galaczi, Director of Research, English, at Cambridge University Press & Assessment, said: "Policymaking has often struggled to keep pace with the rapid rate of technological change, but teachers have had to adapt. This has led to gulfs in knowledge, and an inconsistent approach to AI education and adoption. As often happens, it has become the quiet responsibility of teachers to develop the practical knowledge of what responsible AI integration actually looks like. "Teachers who are already successfully experimenting with AI in their classrooms are prioritising professional judgement, human-centred practices and critical AI literacy. By following this lead, we can ensure AI becomes an effective and responsibly applied tool for teaching and learning, not a crutch for learning shortcuts." NOTES FOR EDITORS 1. Cambridge is committed to sharing research on AI use to support teachers and inform policy. The recommendations in 'Shaping AI Policy and Practice in English Language Teaching' build on three earlier Cambridge papers on AI and teacher use, published to help those working in education navigate and critically evaluate the opportunities and challenges of GenAI: Galaczi, E., & Luckin, R. headline: Segway Powersports Unveils MY27 Lineup and iFUN 2.0 at EICMA 2026, Outlines Global Growth Plans
snippet: MILAN, Nov. 4, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Segway Powersports unveiled its Model Year 2027 (MY27) lineup and next-generation iFUN 2.0 connected system at EICMA 2026. Alongside upgraded ATVs, a flagship two-row UTV and new connected technologies, the company outlined plans to expand its global dealer and service networks. Segway Powersports showcases its MY27 lineup at EICMA 2026 AT6 Pro: More Power, Sharper Control The MY27 AT6 Pro is a key performance model in the lineup. Powertrain and handling improvements give riders more power and greater control. Its 606cc engine, paired with a CVTech transmission, now produces 49 hp. Overall powertrain performance has improved by approximately 15%. To help riders harness that power, electronic throttle control and selectable riding modes allow them to tailor power delivery to changing terrain. AT10: Flagship Power and Performance Built for powerful acceleration and demanding off-road rides, the MY27 AT10 is Segway Powersports' flagship ATV. Its in-house-developed 999cc parallel-twin DOHC engine produces 97 hp and 92 N•m of torque, powering the vehicle from 0 to 100 km/h in eight seconds. Precise valve control supports strong performance at high engine speeds, while the engine's low-vibration design helps keep longer rides comfortable. The AT10 also features iFUN2.0 for a more connected riding experience. Segway Powersports showcases its MY27 ATV lineup with enhanced power and control UT10 Crew Pro: All-Weather Comfort, Every Adventure The UT10 Crew Pro is Segway Powersports' flagship two-row UTV. Its fully enclosed cabin combines automotive-grade sealing with double-layer door seals to help keep dust, moisture and outside noise at bay. Inside, a heating, ventilation and air conditioning (HVAC) system keeps the cabin comfortable. Whether working outdoors or exploring trails with family and friends, drivers and passengers can enjoy a comfortable ride. Steering-wheel controls and iFUN 2.0 put vehicle functions within easy reach. Visitors explore the UT10 Crew Pro’s enclosed cabin designed for all-weather comfort SX20T: Putting Performance to the Test Powered by a 2.0-liter turbocharged engine producing 235 hp, the SX20T is a high-performance sport side-by-side. The model's racing potential was put to the test in multiple competitions worldwide. In 2026, the SX20T made its debut at two major U.S. off-road races: King of the Hammers in February and the Mint 400 in March, finishing third in its group at the latter. In May, it placed second in the T3-N class on the SS2 stage of South America's Desafío Ruta 40, a rally known for its demanding terrain. In Europe, it secured a third-place finish in the SSV category at Portugal's Baja Portalegre 500 in October. At an EICMA ceremony, Segway Powersports also announced its first-ever brand ambassadors: André Rodrigues, Mathias Bellino, Richard Mosna, Nikola Vujnović and Lycett Dayne Christopher. Their experience racing Segway ATVs and SSVs at events worldwide showcases the brand's off-road expertise and vehicle performance. iFUN 2.0: A Smarter, More Connected Ride Developed in-house, iFUN 2.0 brings together six core technologies to simplify vehicle access and control, from preparing for a ride to navigating the trail. Before setting off, riders can check vehicle information through smartphone connectivity and access the vehicle without a physical key using keyless entry. Digital-key sharing lets owners extend that access to family members or riding partners. On the trail, transparent chassis technology reveals the ground beneath the vehicle, helping riders spot obstacles and navigate uneven terrain. Voice control and fingertip controls keep vehicle functions easy to operate, while Bluetooth intercom support lets two riders stay in touch through their helmets. Both the AT10 and UT10 Crew Pro are equipped with iFUN 2.0. Strengthening Global Reach Segway Powersports' global sales network spans more than 65 countries and regions, with over 1,300 retail locations and flagship stores in markets including Spain, Saudi Arabia and Argentina. Building on this presence, the company plans to expand its dealer and service networks to better support customers and dealers worldwide. At EICMA, Segway Powersports will host its biennial global dealer summit, bringing together dealers and distribution partners from around the world to strengthen partnerships and explore new opportunities for growth. The refreshed lineup, in-house-developed technologies and global growth goals reflect Segway Powersports' commitment to enhancing performance, pushing boundaries and inspiring exploration. Together, they embody the brand's "Fear No Place" philosophy and empower riders to go further and conquer new terrain. Beyond performance, Segway Powersports is also forging a distinct visual identity anchored by Rider Red——its signature color-paired with the dedicated Segway Powersports logo. Consistently applied across vehicle designs and brand materials, the color creates a bold, instantly recognizable brand presence. About Segway Powersports Segway Powersports is Segway's professional-grade, high-performance powersports line for global markets. Its vehicles combine power, strong torque, durability and responsive handling for diverse and demanding terrain. The brand operates in more than 65 countries and regions, with over 1,300 retail locations and flagship stores in markets including Spain, Saudi Arabia and Argentina.
